rationale: No matching assumption in WE-056; judged from the text: an uninsured resident who buys analog insulin at about $320 pays $35 instead, and attests at the counter; many of the 4,500 cash buyers will claim.

No matching assumption in WE-056; judged from the text: section 3 fixes what the pharmacy may collect from the covered resident at $35, so the resident's net price falls whatever the pharmacy's posted price.

Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-056 (illustrative figures), A-3: some covered residents used less insulin than prescribed at the old price (2026 survey), so more insulin is dispensed at $35.
No matching assumption in WE-056; judged from the text: every pharmacy stocks insulin and no fixed stock or long lead time is mentioned, so supply is not fixed.
No matching assumption in WE-056; judged from the text: pharmacies can sell the same insulin to cash buyers who are not covered residents; no fixed stock is mentioned.

Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-056 (illustrative figures), A-8: some over-the-counter human insulin buyers obtain a prescription to buy an analog at $35 (the gap of $50 against $35).

Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-056 (illustrative figures), A-25: some individual-market insulin users drop coverage because insulin now costs $35 without it (below the cut-off).
Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-056 (illustrative figures), A-11: some covered residents can defer storable insulin purchases from late 2027 to January 2028.

Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-056 (illustrative figures), A-1: bound pharmacies comply with the $35 cap for most fills and are paid the rest (contract rate, or the Fund's payment).
Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-056 (illustrative figures), A-3: some covered residents used less insulin than prescribed at the old price.
No separate assumption in WE-056; judged from the record: plans did not pay the balance above $35 before the Act, so the term binds (A-1 covers the cap itself, 0.9).
Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-056 (illustrative figures), A-1: bound pharmacies comply and receive the plan's payment.
Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-056 (illustrative figures), A-17: pharmacies, PBMs, insurers and patient groups can organize at a cost below their stakes.
